title: Switch Bounce Debounce Visualizer
description: Two time-aligned strip charts showing a bouncing switch signal and the result of applying a student-chosen debounce delay, with a logical press counter that exposes the too-short-delay failure mode.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Digital Input

learningObjectives: Apply a debounce delay to a noisy switch signal
Demonstrate that too short a delay admits extra press events
Justify a debounce delay given a bounce duration and latency budget
prerequisites: A GPIO pin reads a digital high or low
Reading a pin in a loop

controls.label: Simulate one press
controls.purpose: Generate a new random bounce pattern of 3-6 bounces within 15 ms

controls.label: Show bounce count
controls.purpose: Display raw transitions versus filtered events

simulationModel.modelType: Discrete-time state machine over a sampled signal
assumptions: Bounce activity is confined to the first 15 ms
The signal is sampled every 0.1 ms with no sampling jitter
The press always settles in the pressed state
limitations: Real bounce patterns vary with switch age, contact material, and press force; the release edge also bounces and is not modeled here

keyQuestions: How many logical presses does a 5 ms delay produce?
Why is the press registered later than the physical press?
commonMisconceptions: That a switch closes cleanly once
That any nonzero debounce delay is sufficient
assessmentOpportunities: Choose a debounce delay for a stated bounce duration and justify the latency cost
